A1.justification: Both PDFs describe UGMathBench and contain readable main text, equations, figures, tables, and Appendices A-H. Corresponding content can be matched reliably despite pagination and formatting changes.

before.justification: v1 reports original evaluations of 23 LLMs, including Table 4, subject-level results, error analysis, PHP refinement experiments, and contamination experiments.

after.justification: v2 retains these original empirical results in the main text and appendices. Retained results qualify independently of whether new experiments were added.

M1.justification: Section 5.4 newly reports integrating Xu et al. (2025a)'s model-based evaluator into the repository, adding an answer-evaluation component. Benchmark construction, problem randomization, answer types, and metric definitions remain unchanged.

E1.justification: Both versions use the same English, text-only UGMathBench problems across 16 subjects and three randomized versions, and retain MetaMathQA in the contamination study. Newly cited benchmarks are not newly evaluated datasets.

E2.justification: The same 23 LLMs appear in corresponding main and subject-level comparisons, and PHP comparison coverage is unchanged. The model-based evaluator announcement introduces no reported head-to-head comparison.

E3.justification: v2 reports adding model-based scoring support to the repository beyond the rule-based matching described in Section 4.1. This is a reported evaluation-procedure extension; the published zero-shot settings, 2,048-token limit, and temperature zero remain unchanged, and no rerun is established.

E4.justification: Sections 5.1-5.5 and Appendices D-H retain the same scaling, subject/difficulty/topic, error, PHP refinement, and contamination analyses. No new analysis validates the added evaluator.

E5.justification: Repeated-run, seed, and uncertainty reporting are unchanged. Both retain the same problem-randomization descriptions and point estimates, without adding performance confidence intervals or formal significance tests.

E6.justification: Reported numerical results and findings match throughout, including Table 4's 56.30% EAcc for o1-mini, the contamination results in Table 5, and appendix Tables 13-33. v2 defers updated evaluator results to the repository rather than reporting them in the PDF.

T1.justification: Section 3.3 retains the same mathematical definitions of accuracy, average accuracy, effective accuracy, reasoning gap, and robustness efficiency. Appendix A.1's variation constraints are unchanged in substance; no new derivation or proof appears.

C1.justification: The abstract, introduction, and conclusion retain the same benchmark contribution and claims about benchmark difficulty, reasoning inconsistency, and the gap between evaluated open- and closed-source models.

C2.justification: Interpretations of calculation errors, subject difficulty, refinement effects, and contamination remain unchanged. Both retain the same limitations concerning text-only problems, English-language coverage, and small subject subsets.

D1.justification: v2 adds an explicit code/data repository link in the abstract and documents the model-based evaluator integration in Section 5.4. Existing prompts, deduplication thresholds, training hyperparameters, and hardware disclosures remain unchanged.

R1.justification: v2 adds references to recent benchmarks and reasoning methods, including Omni-MATH, UGPhysics, and Humanity's Last Exam, and credits UGPhysics for the integrated evaluator. The central positioning against existing mathematical benchmarks remains intact.

P1.justification: Findings and research questions change from bullet lists to inline numbered text, alongside limited wording corrections and bibliographic standardization. Main section order and appendix organization remain unchanged.

P2.justification: Figure 1 gains a logo, revised styling, and a distribution heading while retaining its underlying content. Table captions move above table bodies throughout, and Figure 3 is relocated; the remaining plots and table structures are retained.

improvement.justification: The explicit code/data link and documentation of evaluator support modestly improve usability, while added references improve attribution. Scientific claims and empirical evidence remain unchanged, and the PDFs do not demonstrate benefits from the new evaluator, so the overall improvement is limited.
